examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject
provenance_note: Unit text is the published UPSC syllabus for History Paper I, corroborated across independent reproductions. NOT diffed against the notification PDF. Verify before promoting any mention to verified. Every node sets official_syllabus_line_is_verbatim=false, so the ingest records these as mention_type=derived rather than asserting verbatim official text. Set it to true per node only after that node has been diffed against the notification.
structure_note: History Paper I is a flat chronological list of numbered units with no lettered parts, so section_ref is omitted (rev2 M10). Note also that Q1 of this paper is a 20-item map identification question worth 50 marks - the corpus holds only UPSC's locational hints, since the place names live on a map sheet no compilation reproduces. Those questions are flagged requires_map_sheet and will not tag cleanly against any topic here.
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST equal subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-history-p1 exactly.

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1. Sources: Archaeological sources - Exploration, excavation, epigraphy, numismatics, monuments; Literary sources - Indigenous: Primary and secondary; poetry, scientific literature, literature, literature in regional languages, religious literature; Foreign accounts: Greek, Chinese and Arab writers.
micro_themes: Archaeological sources: exploration and excavation
Epigraphy, numismatics and monuments
Indigenous literary sources: primary and secondary
Poetry, scientific and religious literature; regional languages
Foreign accounts: Greek, Chinese and Arab writers

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2. Pre-history and Proto-history: Geographical factors; hunting and gathering (paleolithic and mesolithic); Beginning of agriculture (neolithic and chalcolithic).
micro_themes: Geographical factors in Indian pre-history
Hunting and gathering: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic
Beginning of agriculture: Neolithic and Chalcolithic

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 3. Indus Valley Civilization: Origin, date, extent, characteristics, decline, survival and significance, art and architecture.
micro_themes: Origin, date and extent of the Indus Valley Civilization
Characteristics of the Indus Valley Civilization
Decline, survival and significance
Art and architecture of the Indus Valley Civilization

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 4. Megalithic Cultures: Distribution of pastoral and farming cultures outside the Indus, Development of community life, Settlements, Development of agriculture, Crafts, Pottery, and Iron industry.
micro_themes: Distribution of pastoral and farming cultures outside the Indus
Development of community life and settlements
Development of agriculture and crafts
Pottery and the iron industry

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 5. Aryans and Vedic Period: Expansions of Aryans in India; Vedic Period - Religious and philosophic literature; Transformation from Rig Vedic period to the later Vedic period; Political, social and economic life; Significance of the Vedic Age; Evolution of Monarchy and Varna system.
micro_themes: Expansion of Aryans in India
Religious and philosophic literature of the Vedic period
Transformation from Rig Vedic to later Vedic period
Political, social and economic life in the Vedic age
Significance of the Vedic Age
Evolution of monarchy and the varna system

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 6. Period of Mahajanapadas: Formation of States (Mahajanapada); Republics and monarchies; Rise of urban centres; Trade routes; Economic growth; Introduction of coinage; Spread of Jainism and Buddhism; Rise of Magadha and Nandas; Iranian and Macedonian invasions and their impact.
micro_themes: Formation of states: the Mahajanapadas
Republics and monarchies
Rise of urban centres and trade routes
Economic growth and the introduction of coinage
Spread of Jainism and Buddhism
Rise of Magadha and the Nandas
Iranian and Macedonian invasions and their impact

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 7. Mauryan Empire: Foundation of the Mauryan Empire, Chandragupta, Kautilya and Arthashastra; Ashoka; Concept of Dharma; Edicts; Polity, Administration; Economy; Art, architecture and sculpture; External contacts; Religion; Spread of religion; Literature; Disintegration of the empire; Sungas and Kanvas.
micro_themes: Foundation of the Mauryan empire: Chandragupta, Kautilya and the Arthashastra
Ashoka, the concept of Dharma, and the edicts
Mauryan polity and administration
Mauryan economy
Mauryan art, architecture and sculpture
External contacts, religion and its spread
Literature of the Mauryan period
Disintegration of the empire; Sungas and Kanvas

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 8. Post-Mauryan Period (Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas, Western Kshatrapas): Contact with outside world; growth of urban centres, economy, coinage, development of religions, Mahayana, social conditions, art, architecture, culture, literature and science.
micro_themes: Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas and Western Kshatrapas
Contact with the outside world
Growth of urban centres, economy and coinage
Development of religions; Mahayana Buddhism
Social conditions of the post-Mauryan period
Art, architecture and culture
Literature and science

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 9 Early State and Society in Eastern India, Deccan and South India
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 9. Early State and Society in Eastern India, Deccan and South India: Kharavela, The Satavahanas, Tamil States of the Sangam Age; Administration, economy, land grants, coinage, trade guilds and urban centres; Buddhist centres; Sangam literature and culture; Art and architecture.
micro_themes: Kharavela and the Satavahanas
Tamil states of the Sangam Age
Administration, economy and land grants
Coinage, trade guilds and urban centres
Buddhist centres in the Deccan and South
Sangam literature and culture
Art and architecture of early Deccan and South India

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 10. Guptas, Vakatakas and Vardhanas: Polity and administration, Economic conditions, Coinage of the Guptas, Land grants, Decline of urban centres, Indian feudalism, Caste system, Position of women, Education and educational institutions; Nalanda, Vikramshila and Vallabhi, Literature, scientific literature, art and architecture.
micro_themes: Gupta polity and administration
Economic conditions and Gupta coinage
Land grants, decline of urban centres and Indian feudalism
Caste system and the position of women
Education and educational institutions: Nalanda, Vikramshila, Vallabhi
Literature and scientific literature
Art and architecture of the Gupta age

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 11 Regional States during the Gupta Era
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 11. Regional States during Gupta Era: The Kadambas, Pallavas, Chalukyas of Badami; Polity and Administration, Trade guilds, Literature; growth of Vernacular literature; Education and learning; Arab conquest of Sind; Alberuni; The Chalukyas of Kalyana; Cholas; Hoysalas; Pandyas; Polity and Administration; local Government; Growth of art and architecture, religious sects, Institution of temple and Mathas, Agraharas, education and literature, economy and society.
micro_themes: Kadambas, Pallavas and Chalukyas of Badami
Polity, administration and trade guilds
Growth of vernacular literature; education and learning
Arab conquest of Sind; Alberuni
Chalukyas of Kalyana, Cholas, Hoysalas and Pandyas
Local government in the southern kingdoms
Growth of art and architecture; religious sects
Institution of temple, mathas and agraharas
Economy and society of the regional states

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 12 Themes in Early Indian Cultural History
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 12. Themes in Early Indian Cultural History: Languages and texts, major stages in the evolution of art and architecture, major philosophical thinkers and schools, ideas in Science and Mathematics.
micro_themes: Languages and texts in early India
Major stages in the evolution of art and architecture
Major philosophical thinkers and schools
Ideas in science and mathematics

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 13. Early Medieval India, 750-1200: Polity - Major political developments in Northern India and the Peninsula, origin and the rise of Rajputs; The Cholas - administration, village economy and society; Indian Feudalism; Agrarian economy and urban settlements; Trade and commerce; Society - the status of the Brahman and the new social order; Condition of women; Indian science and technology.
micro_themes: Major political developments in Northern India and the Peninsula
Origin and rise of the Rajputs
The Cholas: administration, village economy and society
Indian feudalism
Agrarian economy and urban settlements
Trade and commerce in early medieval India
Status of the Brahman and the new social order
Condition of women; Indian science and technology

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 14. Cultural Traditions in India, 750-1200: Philosophy - Skankaracharya and Vedanta, Ramanuja and Vishishtadvaita, Madhva and Brahma-Mimansa; Religion - Forms and features of religion, Tamil devotional cult, growth of Bhakti, Islam and its arrival in India, Sufism; Literature - Literature in Sanskrit, growth of Tamil literature, literature in the newly developing languages, Kalhan's Rajtarangini, Alberuni's India; Art and Architecture - Temple architecture, sculpture, painting.
micro_themes: Shankaracharya and Vedanta; Ramanuja and Vishishtadvaita; Madhva
Forms and features of religion; the Tamil devotional cult
Growth of Bhakti
Islam and its arrival in India; Sufism
Literature in Sanskrit and the growth of Tamil literature
Literature in newly developing languages; Rajatarangini and Alberuni's India
Temple architecture, sculpture and painting

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 15. The Thirteenth Century: Establishment of the Delhi Sultanate; The Ghurian invasions - factors behind Ghurian success; Economic, Social and cultural consequences; Foundation of Delhi Sultanate and early Turkish Sultans; Consolidation - The rule of Iltutmish and Balban.
micro_themes: The Ghurian invasions and factors behind Ghurian success
Economic, social and cultural consequences of the invasions
Foundation of the Delhi Sultanate and the early Turkish Sultans
Consolidation under Iltutmish and Balban

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 16. The Fourteenth Century: 'The Khalji Revolution'; Alauddin Khalji - Conquests and territorial expansion, agrarian and economic measures; Muhammad Tughluq - Major projects, agrarian measures, bureaucracy of Muhammad Tughluq; Firuz Tughluq - Agrarian measures, achievements in civil engineering and public works, decline of the Sultanate, foreign contacts and Ibn Battuta's account.
micro_themes: The Khalji Revolution
Alauddin Khalji: conquests, territorial expansion, agrarian and economic measures
Muhammad Tughluq: major projects, agrarian measures and bureaucracy
Firuz Tughluq: agrarian measures, civil engineering and public works
Decline of the Sultanate; foreign contacts and Ibn Battuta's account

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 17 Society, Culture and Economy in the Thirteenth and Fourteenth Centuries
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 17. Society, Culture and Economy in the Thirteenth and Fourteenth Centuries: Society - composition of rural society, ruling classes, town dwellers, women, religious classes, caste and slavery under the Sultanate, Bhakti movement, Sufi movement; Culture - Persian literature, literature in the regional languages of North India, literature in the languages of South India, Sultanate architecture and new structural forms, painting, evolution of a composite culture; Economy - Agricultural Production, rise of urban economy and non-agricultural production, trade and commerce.
micro_themes: Composition of rural society; ruling classes and town dwellers
Women, religious classes, caste and slavery under the Sultanate
Bhakti movement and Sufi movement
Persian literature and regional literatures of North India
Literature in the languages of South India
Sultanate architecture and new structural forms; painting
Evolution of a composite culture
Agricultural production; rise of the urban economy
Non-agricultural production, trade and commerce

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 18 The Fifteenth and Early Sixteenth Century - Political Developments and Economy
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 18. The Fifteenth and early Sixteenth Century - Political Developments and Economy: Rise of Provincial Dynasties - Bengal, Kashmir (Zainul Abedin), Gujarat, Malwa, Bahmanids; The Vijayanagra Empire; Lodis; Mughal Empire, First phase - Babur and Humayun; The Sur Empire - Sher Shah's administration; Portuguese colonial enterprise; Bhakti and Sufi Movements.
micro_themes: Rise of provincial dynasties: Bengal, Kashmir, Gujarat, Malwa, Bahmanids
The Vijayanagara Empire
The Lodis
Mughal Empire first phase: Babur and Humayun
The Sur Empire and Sher Shah's administration
Portuguese colonial enterprise
Bhakti and Sufi movements in this period

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 19 The Fifteenth and Early Sixteenth Century - Society and Culture
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 19. The Fifteenth and early Sixteenth Century - Society and Culture: Regional cultural specificities; literary traditions; provincial architecture; society, culture, literature and the arts in Vijayanagara Empire.
micro_themes: Regional cultural specificities and literary traditions
Provincial architecture
Society, culture, literature and the arts in the Vijayanagara Empire

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 20. Akbar: Conquests and consolidation of the Empire; Establishment of Jagir and Mansab systems; Rajput policy; Evolution of religious and social outlook, theory of Sulh-i-kul and religious policy; Court patronage of art and technology.
micro_themes: Conquests and consolidation of the empire
Establishment of the jagir and mansab systems
Rajput policy
Evolution of religious and social outlook; Sulh-i-kul and religious policy
Court patronage of art and technology

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 21 Mughal Empire in the Seventeenth Century
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 21. Mughal Empire in the Seventeenth Century: Major administrative policies of Jahangir, Shahjahan and Aurangzeb; The Empire and the Zamindars; Religious policies of Jahangir, Shahjahan and Aurangzeb; Nature of the Mughal State; Late Seventeenth century crisis and the revolts; The Ahom Kingdom; Shivaji and the early Maratha Kingdom.
micro_themes: Administrative policies of Jahangir, Shahjahan and Aurangzeb
The Empire and the zamindars
Religious policies of Jahangir, Shahjahan and Aurangzeb
Nature of the Mughal state
Late seventeenth century crisis and the revolts
The Ahom kingdom
Shivaji and the early Maratha kingdom

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 22 Economy and Society in the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Centuries
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 22. Economy and Society in the 16th and 17th Centuries: Population, agricultural production, craft production; Towns; Commerce with Europe through Dutch, English and French companies; a trade revolution; Indian mercantile classes, banking, insurance and credit systems; Condition of peasants, Condition of Women; Evolution of the Sikh community and the Khalsa Panth.
micro_themes: Population, agricultural production and craft production
Towns in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries
Commerce with Europe through the Dutch, English and French companies
The trade revolution
Indian mercantile classes; banking, insurance and credit systems
Condition of peasants and condition of women
Evolution of the Sikh community and the Khalsa Panth

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 23. Culture in the Mughal Empire: Persian histories and other literature; Hindi and religious literatures; Mughal architecture; Mughal painting; Provincial architecture and painting; Classical music; Science and technology.
micro_themes: Persian histories and other literature
Hindi and religious literatures
Mughal architecture
Mughal painting
Provincial architecture and painting
Classical music
Science and technology under the Mughals

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 24. The Eighteenth Century: Factors for the decline of the Mughal Empire; The regional principalities - Nizam's Deccan, Bengal, Awadh; Maratha ascendancy under the Peshwas; The Maratha fiscal and financial system; Emergence of Afghan Power and Battle of Panipat; State of politics, culture and economy on the eve of the British conquest.
micro_themes: Factors for the decline of the Mughal Empire
Regional principalities: Nizam's Deccan, Bengal, Awadh
Maratha ascendancy under the Peshwas
The Maratha fiscal and financial system
Emergence of Afghan power and the Battle of Panipat
Politics, culture and economy on the eve of the British conquest
